Piricse Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Dózsa György utca 26, Hungary

Not demolished. Piricse's Jewish community, settled from the beginning of the 19th century, joined the Orthodox stream in 1867 and built a synagogue around the mid-19th century; in the 1940s, its shochet, Sámuel Grosz, also served as community leader. In 1944, following the German occupation, Piricse's Jews were taken to the Nyíregyháza Ghetto, then the nearby Nyírgespuszta Ghetto, before deportation to Auschwitz on May 25; the synagogue was used as a stable during the war. Eleven survivors returned but did not revive the community, soon leaving the village. This cemetery was established as early as 1870, per that year's cadastral map.
